title: Systematic, zero and random errors practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numbers, apparatus settings and figure briefs are newly authored. The mapped P2 leaves ground same-direction offsets, random scatter, analogue reading variation, instrument selection, repeated wire measurements and apparatus-specific systematic faults. Complete source-question contexts were reviewed so later-topic demands remain excluded.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct Lesson 5 retrieval, error-pattern recognition, signed zero correction, remedy selection, a wire-measurement procedure, a corrected repeated-mass calculation, then a mixed homogeneity and measurement-error application

questions.prompt: From the previous lesson, state the condition that makes a physical equation homogeneous and state the limited conclusion that follows when an equation passes this check.
A student measures the same steady quantity five times and obtains values on both sides of a central value, with no fixed direction to the variation. Which description best fits this pattern?

options.A: A systematic error shifts every reading upward
options.B: A random error varies unpredictably between readings
options.C: A positive zero error is identical in every reading
options.D: The physical equation used is not homogeneous

questions.prompt: A digital balance reads +0.04 g when empty. It displays 7.86 g with an object on it. Which corrected mass follows from this zero check?
Which action is most suitable for reducing the effect of random variation when measuring an unchanging quantity?

options.A: Take one reading and add the instrument zero reading
options.B: Take repeated readings and calculate their mean
options.C: Change the unit written beside the reading
options.D: Use the same single reading several times in a calculation

questions.prompt: A student must determine a representative diameter for a thin wire.

figure.purpose: Establish the physical context and small scale of the wire without suggesting any measurement choice or procedure
figure.brief: Create an original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular line drawing of one plain thin wire sample lying on an otherwise empty white field. Use a simple close view so the wire appears slender. Include no instrument, scale, dimensions, labels, marked positions, arrows, displays, zero-reading cue or procedural annotation.
figure.alt_text: A plain close view of a slender wire sample.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Name a suitable instrument for measuring the diameter.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe how the student should check for a zero error and state how a non-zero result would affect all uncorrected diameter readings.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe how measurements should be taken and processed to reduce the effect of random variation and represent the wire as a whole.

questions.prompt: An empty balance displays +0.06 g. Five indicated readings for the same sample are 18.42 g, 18.47 g, 18.45 g, 18.44 g and 18.46 g.

figure.purpose: Present the zero check and repeated readings in a clear apparatus record without showing the processing
figure.brief: Create an original black-and-white rectangular laboratory record card. Show an empty balance display +0.06 g and a separate five-cell row containing 18.42, 18.47, 18.45, 18.44 and 18.46 g. Do not add a mean, subtraction, labels for error type or final result.
figure.alt_text: An empty balance reads plus 0.06 grams and five sample readings range from 18.42 to 18.47 grams.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify the error shown by the empty balance and explain why it belongs to that error type.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean indicated reading and then determine the corrected mean mass.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why averaging helps with the variation among the five readings but does not by itself remove the zero error.

questions.prompt: A timing system uses the supplied model R = L/t. The reported quantity R has unit m s^-1, length L has unit m and time t has unit s. A stationary zero check gives +0.004 s. Five indicated times for one repeated event are 0.204 s, 0.202 s, 0.206 s, 0.203 s and 0.205 s.

figure.purpose: Join an earlier-module unit check to a current measurement-error record without revealing either conclusion
figure.brief: Create an original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular timing-system card. Show R = L/t with the three supplied units, a zero-check display +0.004 s and a five-cell time table. Do not simplify units, calculate a mean, apply a correction or name error types.
figure.alt_text: A timing-system card gives a model and units, a positive zero reading and five repeated time readings.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use SI base units to test whether the supplied model is homogeneous.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean indicated time and then apply the signed zero correction to determine the corrected mean time.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State which feature of the data is addressed by averaging and which feature requires the separate correction. Explain each choice.
